## Part 99: the game data install dialog — the disc's INSDIR copied to the memory stick, a piece at each Update, through a folder of its own; sceIoChstat (Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep Final Mix's DATA INSTALL)

On branch `cursor/psp-gamedata-install-2b67` (draft PR #261), on master `cc0638372` (part 97, #259, after part 95,
#257), with master `6ff82f9f1` merged in after the fifth round (parts 96, #258, and 98, #260). Deep play batch 04's
bug 3: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep Final Mix's DATA INSTALL ended in "An error has occurred. Data installation will
be canceled.", and Gunhound EX's was cancelled too,
because part 37 had made the system's game data install dialog one that runs and is cancelled. Clean room: the PSP's
behaviour from pspautotests' recordings (utility/dialog/sizes: the dialog's two sizes; io/stat and io/stat/readonly:
sceIoChstat and the memory stick's attributes), players' reports of Kingdom Hearts' install failing on real PSPs
(GameFAQs' and Reddit's "The Memory Stick could not be accessed (80111904)"), the games' own code (Kingdom Hearts'
traced and disassembled from a dump of its memory) and discs (every INSDIR in the library listed), and PPSSPP's
`PSPGamedataInstallDialog`, its error codes and its notes on sceIoChstat read only as a description of the PSP, nothing
copied or translated. JPCSP was not read; a web search's results showed, unasked, a few lines of one of its files,
among them a name for 0x80111902. Nothing is taken from them: that code is chosen below from the pattern of the codes
the clean sources give. Save states: unchanged (layout 32): the copy isn't state.

**What Kingdom Hearts does.** Title > DATA INSTALL > OK > 200 MB > Yes. The game asks the savedata utility's size mode
about "ULJM05775DATA" (NO_DATA: none yet), then starts the install dialog with 0x598 bytes of parameters: mode 0, the
game "ULJM05775", the data "DATA", the titles "Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep -Final Mix-", "Install Data" and
"Deleting this will cause load times to increase.", parental level 1. It reads the dialog's progress (a getter at
0x088d76c8, for its own install screen) and, once the dialog's gone, only its result: ≥ 0 goes on. Its disc's INSDIR
holds ICON0.PNG and PIC1.PNG alone, the install's icons; the data is the game's to copy. A thread of its own
("DataInstall") then registers a memory stick callback, looks at ms0:/PSP, PSP/SAVEDATA and the install's folder with
sceIoGetstat, taking the read-only flag off any that has it with sceIoChstat, and copies
disc0:/PSP_GAME/USRDIR/BBS1.DAT (206,092,288 bytes) into the folder half a MiB at a time, each piece after another
sceIoChstat on the file. sceIoChstat was missing (the kernel's "not yet
linked", 0x8002013a), and the game takes any failure there for the memory stick failing: it empties and removes the
folder and shows the system's message with **0x80111904**, the code players saw on real PSPs with bad memory sticks.
Cancelled (part 37), the thread found no folder and gave its own error.

**What a PSP's dialog does.** Its parameters (0x590 or 0x598 bytes: utility/dialog/sizes; the layout PPSSPP's notes
give, and Kingdom Hearts' code fills): the common part; at 48 the mode, 1 for the PSP's own progress screen, 0 (or
less) for none, the game drawing its own; at 52 the game's name (13 bytes) and at 68 the data's (20); at 88 the
install's titles as a save's sfoParam (the title in 128 bytes, the data's own title at 216, its detail in 1024 at 344,
the parental level at 1368); at 1372 the progress, 0 to 100, kept current as it copies; what follows is unknown (PPSSPP
writes the files' count into the next two words, marked as not understood; Kingdom Hearts never reads them: left as the
game has them). It copies every file of the disc's PSP_GAME/INSDIR into the memory stick's PSP/SAVEDATA/<game><data>
and writes a PARAM.SFO there describing the install as a save's describes it (TITLE, SAVEDATA_TITLE, SAVEDATA_DETAIL,
PARENTAL_LEVEL, CATEGORY "MS", SAVEDATA_DIRECTORY), keeping a PARAM.SFO's other keys; over a folder already there it
writes the same files over the ones there (PPSSPP's notes; Kingdom Hearts and Gunhound EX ask "already installed,
overwrite?" first, and Gunhound EX's install asked again goes on to write it over). No clean-room recording covers
that merge: it's kept as PPSSPP's notes describe it and the games expect it. Its statuses are a dialog's: starting,
running while it copies, finished, shutting down.

**The change** (`install.cpp`, new; `utility.cpp`'s Update; `kernel.cpp`, `kernel.hpp`, `serialization.cpp`).
- At its first Update the dialog lists INSDIR's files (folders in it aren't copied), from the disc image or a host
  folder standing for the disc, and checks the request; then each Update copies a piece, 1 MiB
  (`InstallBytesPerUpdate`: a fixed amount, so a run takes as many Updates every time; 22 to 27 ms a piece from a CHD
  on the Mac while it was shared), writes the progress and, once every file is there, makes it the save's folder. The
  statuses and timing are the other dialogs': 200 ms starting, 40 ms closing.
- **What it writes, and what it may write over** (the PSP's dialog would write the same): the folder
  PSP/SAVEDATA/<game><data>; in it INSDIR's files and PARAM.SFO, over the files of those names already there. Nothing
  else in that folder is touched, and nothing anywhere else on the memory stick but its own copy folder, below.
  PARAM.SFO comes from INSDIR's own if it has one, else the folder's, else afresh (a broken one afresh), with the
  request's TITLE, SAVEDATA_TITLE, SAVEDATA_DETAIL, PARENTAL_LEVEL, CATEGORY and SAVEDATA_DIRECTORY, and (chosen, as
  every save Phobos writes has them) a SAVEDATA_FILE_LIST and SAVEDATA_PARAMS if it lacks them.
- **Through a folder of its own.** The copy is made in `<memory stick>/.phobos-install/<game><data>` and becomes the
  save's folder by one rename once every file and PARAM.SFO are written; where the folder is there already, each file
  is moved into it over the one of its name, PARAM.SFO last. Programs can neither see nor reach that folder
  (`io.cpp`): `resolve()` answers "not found" for any memory stick path whose first name is `.phobos-install`,
  whatever its case, with dots or spaces at its end (which Windows and Linux's FAT driver drop from a name), and
  however the path is written (`fatms0:`, `..`, from the working folder); and for any path whose real place, links
  followed, is in it, compared by name and as a file (`std::filesystem::equivalent`), so a link to it or a short 8.3
  name a FAT host gives it doesn't reach it either. So no game can open, make, remove or rename anything in it, and
  sceIoDopen of the stick's top leaves it out; the savedata utility looks in PSP/SAVEDATA alone. (Without this, a
  game's sceIoRemove and sceIoRmdir took a running install's copy away on `1fbabdf43`, below.) Phobos stopped part
  way (killed, the machine reset, the game aborting the dialog, a state loaded) leaves the saves as they were, never
  a half folder a game would take for its install: the savedata utility
  still says NO_DATA for it. Aborted, reset or a state loaded, the copies' folder is taken away at once, with all it
  holds (`installAbandon()`, by the folder's own name, as below). As one install runs at a
  time, whatever is in `.phobos-install` when an install starts, or when the memory stick is put in at power on
  (`mount()`, after the kernel's power has given up any install), is a copy left so, and all of it is taken away
  (`installLeftovers()`): a phone that killed Phobos part way through 7th Dragon 2020's 1.5 GB gets the room back at
  the next boot. That takes away `<stick>/.phobos-install` and nothing else: links in it are taken away and never
  followed; a link in its place is taken away itself at power on, and an install that finds one there gives up
  (0x80111904) with nothing behind it touched; and where something in it can't be taken away (no permission), the
  install answers 0x80111904 before anything is written, PSP/SAVEDATA untouched.
- **The copy checked as it goes.** Only the host can change the copy (programs can't reach it), but a host may: a tool
  keeping the memory stick in step with another device's, say, that mirrors that device's power-on cleanup. Before
  each piece the copy must be as the install left it: nothing yet before a file's first piece, and after that a file
  of its own (not a link) as long as what's been copied. At the end, before PARAM.SFO is written, every file must be a
  file of its own as long as the disc's. Otherwise the install gives up with 0x80111904 and the copy is taken away,
  as when a write fails. Before this, later pieces were added at whatever end a file had: a copy taken away after
  the first piece was made again and installed 1.5 MiB of the test's 2.5 MiB, answered 0. A link in a copy's place
  would have been written through, its target off the stick added to or cut short. Before each piece and at the end,
  the copy's folder and the copies' folder it's in must also be real folders, not links (`installFolderIntact()`):
  a host that put a link to a folder off the stick there would have had the next file made in that folder. And the
  cleanup takes the whole copies' folder away by its own name, as the power-on cleanup does, so a link put in its
  place, even while the cleanup runs, is taken away itself and nothing through it. Taking the copy's folder away by
  its path instead looked the copies' folder up on the way, and through a link swapped in meanwhile: the reviewer's
  host thread swapping it had Phobos take away a folder of the copy's name off the stick 12 times in 6,524 cleanups,
  and none in 4,177 with this.
- **Not state.** The copy's place isn't in a save state (so no layout change, and every state the same as master's):
  loading a state takes the copy's folder away, and an install running in the loaded state starts again at its next
  Update, its progress from 0. Phobos never loads states behind the player's back (the stored "run ahead" setting is
  used nowhere), so an install only starts again where the player loaded a state.
- **Its answers**, at 28: **0**, installed. **1**, cancelled: the game's sceUtilityGamedataInstallAbort (Kingdom
  Hearts' code calls it on flags of its own), the copy taken away; and, chosen, a disc with nothing to install (no
  INSDIR, or nothing but folders in it), answered first, as the dialog answered every install before this part.
  **0x80111901**, no memory stick (PPSSPP's notes' MEMSTICK_REMOVED). **0x80111902**, not enough free space: chosen,
  from the pattern of the codes known, as nothing clean-room records it: the save group's 0x80110382 to 0x80110385 are
  removed, no space, protected and access, as the install's 0x80111901, 0x80111903 (PPSSPP's notes' WRITE_PROTECTED)
  and 0x80111904 are removed, protected and access. **0x80111904**, the memory stick couldn't be written (the players'
  reports above); chosen too for names that would lead out of SAVEDATA, a folder's name ending in '.' or ' ' (FAT and
  Windows drop those, so "DATA." would go into DATA's folder on one host and be a folder of its own on another), a
  file where the folder goes (found at the first Update, before anything is copied, and looked at again at the end),
  a copy left before that can't be taken away, a copy the host changed meanwhile, a write failing with room on the
  host, and the disc failing to read.
  **0x80111908**, a mode of 2 or more (PPSSPP's notes). The free space is the memory stick's as every function tells
  it (io.cpp's 57,344 free clusters of 32 KiB): the install takes each file in whole clusters, one for PARAM.SFO and
  one for the folder, as savedata's sizes count a save, and more than the free clusters is no space before anything is
  written. Where the host itself hasn't room for the copy and 64 MiB more (a phone's storage nearly full), the same
  answer: an install never fills the host's storage; and where a write fails with the host short of that room
  (something else filling it while the copy runs), the same answer again, the copy taken away and its room given
  back. Every install in the library fits (the largest INSDIR, 7th Dragon 2020's translation, is 1,532,651,653 bytes:
  46,776 clusters with its PARAM.SFO and folder).
- **The trailing '.' and ' ' check is the install's alone.** The savedata utility's names go through the same check of
  plain names (`utility.cpp`'s `plainName()`, used by its save, load, size and list modes and its dialogs), and
  refusing such names there could keep a game from loading or writing a save it already has, so they're left as they
  were. Deep play's savedata traces (`~/phobos-work/deepplay`, 1,296 savedata calls) name no game, save or file
  ending so, but they don't cover the library.
- **sceIoChstat** (`io.cpp`, new): as io/stat/readonly recorded, the mode's write bits and the attributes' 0x01 are one
  read-only flag on a PSP's memory stick file (made 0444 a file reads mode 0x216d and attributes 0x21, made 0777 again
  0x21ff and 0x20, given the attributes 0x21 alone the same as 0444, each change answered 0). Here the flag is the host
  file's owner's write permission (made writable, the owner's alone is given back). Where both are named the
  attributes say which: chosen, as the recording names both only once, agreeing. The recording has a file's flag
  alone: a folder's is answered 0 and changed nowhere (chosen: a host folder that can't be written takes no new files,
  while Windows' and Linux's FAT drivers ignore a folder's flag, so a game setting it on PSP/SAVEDATA would otherwise
  stop every save), and a folder never reads read-only. The device's top (`ms0:/`, `ms0:`, `fatms0:/`) is refused as
  sceIoGetstat refuses it (io/stat: "ms0:" 0x80010016). The rest of a status (times, size, private words) is answered
  0 and left. On the disc, ErrorReadOnly. And sceIoGetstat and sceIoDread give a stick file's attributes as io/stat
  recorded them, FAT's: 0x20 a file, 0x10 a folder, 0x01 more and the mode's write bits gone where a file is
  read-only. They had been 0x27 and 0x17, which as FAT's attributes say read-only, hidden and system. Kingdom Hearts
  reads its three folders' status and sets the attributes alone (bits 0x2) only where they say read-only: given the
  old 0x17 it passed 0x16, 0x17 without read-only, for ms0:/PSP, PSP/SAVEDATA and its folder (`kh/run-v2`, whose
  runner still had the old attributes); given 0x10, as a PSP gives, it changes no folder (`kh/run-r2`, the second
  round's code). BBS1.DAT it gives 0 before each piece. (The disc's files are as before.)
- **A front end** (the option "Dialogs", part 73): in mode 1, where a PSP shows its progress screen, the dialog posts a
  request of a kind of its own (7), made afresh as the progress moves on, which takes no answer: its mode 1, its focus
  the progress, and its one save the install (the data's name, the titles, the bytes it copies, INSDIR's ICON0.PNG,
  whether the folder's there). The app (`PspSystemDialogs.kt`'s `PspInstallDialog`) shows the icon, titles and size
  and "Installing… N%" over the game, with no button and no back (the install can't be stopped there; the core takes
  it down as it finishes); its pause hotkey still pauses. In mode 0 nothing is posted, as a PSP shows nothing.
  Without a front end (the runner, the tests, the desktop and libretro hosts) the install runs the same, drawing
  nothing, as the runner's other dialogs draw nothing.

**Left, and why.**

  that room go once the PGD layer reads stick files, its own task now (the PGD and NPDRM code is open to agents since
  2026-10-15, the owner approving); part 97 lists it too. Done since, in part 101.

  seconds here), the words after the progress, its answer for no space (0x80111902 is the pattern's) or for a disc
  with nothing to install (cancelled is the stub's answer, kept), or what it does over an install there (the merge
  is PPSSPP's description).

  says a PSP's has one.

  read-only flag isn't kept (chosen, above).
- A short 8.3 name for the copies' folder is kept out by comparing files, which wasn't tried on a host that makes such
  names (Windows, Linux's FAT driver): the Mac's file systems have none. The tests try the dots and spaces, the cases
  and the links.
- The copy is checked by its files' lengths, not their bytes: a host that put other bytes of the same length in a
  file of the copy would go unseen.
- A write can still race a host (the reviewer's, informational): a link swapped into the copies' folder's place, or
  the copy's folder's, in the microseconds between the folder check and a file's opening has that file's first piece
  written through the link, onto a file of the same name behind it if there is one. The checks narrow it to that
  window. Closing it fully needs openat-style I/O (each name opened in a folder already held open, never looked up
  again), which `std::filesystem` and the streams don't give.

## Part 100: the GE's per-PRIM paths on the RP6's Cortex-X3 — a PRIM's kept settings compared where they are, fast mode's screen triangles without calls (GE round 4, part A)

On branch `cursor/psp-ge-round4a-2b67` (draft PR #262), on master `cc0638372` (part 97, #259), with masters `02cd1fa8c`
(part 98, #260), `6ff82f9f1` (part 96, #258) and `462f8ff2f` (part 99, #261) merged in. Clean room: no PPSSPP code read
(its GPU backend not opened), JPCSP not read. Nothing of the PSP's behaviour changes: the host's work for each PRIM and
each triangle, the same draws in the same order, so Vulkan (fast), Vulkan (accurate) and the software renderer draw the
same frames, VRAM, RAM and machine state as master (checked below). Save states unchanged (no field added).

**The problem.** The coordinator's bisect on the RP6 (14 Oct, the headless runner built for Android (#255), the
emulation thread, Vulkan fast, 600 frames, medians of three rounds taking turns; `runner-android/runs/sb-*`): #253 (part
92) took 1.4% of the instructions out of Super Monkey Ball's story scene (50,000 PRIMs a frame) but added 3.3% cycles
and 2.5% CPU time; Chains of Olympus's difficulty menu −1.3% instructions, +1.9% cycles, +4.5% CPU time; #254 (part 93)
0.6% more cycles in Monkey Ball. On the Mac's M1 #253 was a clear win. The X3's counters (each beside the pinned
instructions and cycles in turns, scaled): Monkey Ball's frontend stalls rose from 8.3% to 10.1% of its cycles, two
thirds of the cycles added, while its backend stalls (16.2% → 16.0%), mispredicts (0.79 → 0.72 a thousand instructions)
and data refills (1.99 → 1.89) didn't; L1I refills 3.2 → 3.4 (and 6.0 with #254, its frontend share unchanged). The
instructions' supply, not the data.

**What the X3 ran** (master's Android build, its symbols, `llvm-objdump`; how often from a counting build on the Mac,
`paths-patch.py`, a frame):
- Monkey Ball: 50,306 PRIMs begun, 97.6% of them keeping their settings; 91,333 triangles of its small PRIMs drawn
  among the meshes (screen triangles, part 92); 1,763 meshes. Ghost of Sparta's menu 18,514 PRIMs and 51,056 screen
  triangles; Chains of Olympus 6,121 and 11,902; Army of Two 5,657 and 4,491 (and 638,000 mesh models); Killzone's
  gameplay 1,182 PRIMs, their settings kept for 149.
- **The kept check**, at the head of `settings()`: a 276-byte key built on the stack at each PRIM (the PixelState
  copied in with sixteen-byte stores), compared by a call to bionic's `memcmp` through the PLT and then field by
  field, a branch each, all inside `settings()`'s frame: twelve registers saved, 608 bytes, the stack protector's
  canary (the app's builds have `-fstack-protector-strong`). A key that differed was copied whole (`memcpy`, another
  PLT call).
- **Each screen triangle** (`screenTriangle()`, inlined into `triangleAt()`): four calls. `meshState()` (its whole
  prologue and canary even where the state was kept, around a ten-instruction answer), the models' and the indices'
  `resize()` (libc++'s `vector::__append`, the indices zeroed before they were written), `meshDraw()`. Before #253
  such a triangle was one call (`emit()`).
- **The X3's own profile** (`rp6-profile.sh` at the session's end, below: simpleperf sampling cycles and frontend
  stalls in Monkey Ball, master's run) names them: `settings()` 2.7% of the emulation thread's cycles, libc's
  `memcmp` 1.3%, the screen triangle's calls 4.0% (`vector::__append` 1.7%, `meshState()` 1.2%, `meshDraw()` 1.1%),
  `memset` 0.3%.

**The changes** (`20d0ae180`, `88cbac19e`, `d5b5ec227`):
1. **The kept settings compared where they are** (`GPU::kept()`): the PixelState's 208 bytes as they're laid out
   (its padding too, as `memcmp` compared it) in sixteen-byte lanes, XORed and ORed, and the key's other inputs (the
   texture's size and clamps, its function, environment and alpha, the write masks, the target, its rows and the
   frame buffer's place in it, the shading and filter, the backend's ways of drawing) likewise, with a branch at the
   end alone. `settings()` is the work done where they differ, a call of its own (`NALL_NOINLINE`), and records them
   (`keptSettings`). The key has every input it had: a PRIM keeps its settings exactly where master's did. It starts
   zeroed with the renderer, as `kept()` reads each field before it looks at `valid` (the checks below).
   `meshDrawable()` answers once for a PRIM's settings while they're kept (`drawableKnown`, cleared by `settings()`,
   the one place the pipeline changes), not with a hash of the pipeline at each mesh. #254's blending by the frame
   buffer's alpha is decided with the settings (`blendsByAlpha`), from the bits the key holds.
2. **`meshState()` and `meshDraw()`** keep their kept and joining paths inline; what records a new state or a new
   draw is out of line (`recordMeshState()`, `newMeshDraw()`).
3. **The recording's models and indices are piles** (`GPU::Pile<T>`): an append is a bound's check and a sum, the room
   made larger out of line (`NALL_NOINLINE`) and kept as the recording's cleared, as a vector's capacity was; the
   backend reads them as it read the vectors (`size()`, `empty()`, `data()`). A screen triangle's hot code on the X3
   makes no call now (what's left out of line comes after the function's return). `mesh()` no longer zeroes the
   indices it writes over (2 MB a frame in Army of Two). Tried first: `emplace_back()` and `push_back()`, which libc++
   compiled with each one's reallocation inline: six blocks in `triangleAt()` (2,508 → 3,540 bytes), each jumped
   over at each triangle. Replaced before the RP6 measured it; `triangleAt()` is 2,580 bytes now.

**Numbers.** The Mac (M1, MoltenVK, the bench runner at -O3 with thin LTO, 300 frames from each scene's state, the
emulation thread a frame, medians of two rounds taking turns; master `cc0638372` → `88cbac19e`): Super Monkey Ball
427.1 → 407.6 M instructions (−4.6%), 34.96 → 33.71 ms (−3.6%); Ghost of Sparta 302.2 → 293.3 (−2.9%), 22.50 → 21.93

## Part 101: PGD files on the memory stick — a game's installed data read through the PGD layer (Gunhound EX, 7th Dragon 2020), the PGD layer's answers to a wrong key, a damaged header and a write, and the disc's seek request in an unlocked PGD's data

On branch `cursor/psp-pgd-stick-2b67` (draft PR #263), on master `6ff82f9f1` (part 96, #258, after part 98, #260),
with master `462f8ff2f` (part 99, #261, the game data install dialog) and then `1c75c5600` (part 100, #262) merged
in for the review's round. Part 99's "Left" item, the PGD layer on memory stick files, is this part. The first work in
the PGD/NPDRM code since the owner opened it to
agents on 15 Oct 2026 (the handoff's standing note): agents write and maintain `pgd.cpp`, `pgd.hpp`, io.cpp's
sceNpDrm functions, its PGD requests and the EDATA path, and the owner approves their PRs as any other. Clean room:
the PSP's behaviour from "tpu"'s decompilation of the firmware's PGD layer (kirk_engine's `npdrm/dnas_ida.c`, the
module iofilemgr_dnas, part 97's source), uOFW's `iofilemgr_kernel.h` and `errors.h` (the flag's, the key request's
and ENOTSUP's names) and the games themselves; PPSSPP's `sceIo.cpp` read only as a description of the PSP (its PGD key
request's answers), nothing copied or translated; JPCSP not read. `pgd.cpp`'s own crypto, two of its checks given
names. Save states: unchanged (no field added).

**The problem.** #261's game data install dialog (part 99) copies a disc's PSP_GAME/INSDIR to the memory stick, as a
PSP's does. Gunhound EX (NPJH50723) installs 797 files (460 MB), every one a PGD, to
`ms0:/PSP/SAVEDATA/NPJH5072300INST00`; on its next boot it opens each it wants (00000313.DAT first, which stands for
the disc's DRQ/FIRST/DASHBOARDPSP.TGA) with 0x40000001 and gives it its key (ioctl 0x04100001). 7th Dragon 2020
(NPJH50459) installs GAME.DNS (1.53 GB) to NPJH50459USERID and opens it the same way (0x40004001). io.cpp refused every
request on a file off the disc (0x8001b000, ENOTSUP), so Gunhound EX failed to read its install and loaded from the
disc, and 7th Dragon 2020 said "The installed data could not be read. Data installation will be turned OFF. Installed
data will be read from the UMD." All 30 discs in the library with an INSDIR import the install dialog; any of them
that reads its install through the PGD layer was the same (Black Wolves Saga looks for
`ms0:/psp/SAVEDATA/ULJM06220DAT/INSTALL.DNS` so at boot). And the disc's own seek request (ioctl 0x01010005) bounded an
unlocked PGD by its file's size, where every other seek of one stops at its data's end since part 97.

**What a PSP does** (tpu's decompilation of iofilemgr_dnas, which the firmware adds to the I/O manager as a hook,
`sceIoAddHook`, the "gamedata" driver):
- Its match takes any file opened with 0x40000000 (uOFW's SCE_FGAMEDATA) and tests no device: a memory stick file
  opened so is the PGD layer's as a disc file is, and answers its requests (0x04100001 the key, 0x04100002 where the
  PGD starts, 0x04100010 the data's size) as a disc file does. A request it doesn't know goes on to the device's
  driver.
- Its open refuses a file opened so to write (0x80510201, SCE_GAMEDATA_ERROR_INVALID_ARG), before the device sees it.
- The key request reads the 0x90-byte header where the PGD starts and checks, in order: the magic "\0PGD" (else
  0x80510204, INVALID_FORMAT); the header's version (0x80510205) and its DNAS MAC at 0x80 (0x80510204); its 0x70 MAC
  against the key given (0x80510206, SECURE_INSTALL_ID: no key is recovered); then the descriptor's version and block
  size (0x80510205, 0x80510204) and the MAC of the block MACs' table (0x80510207). A header shorter than 0x90 bytes:
  0x80510204. Refused, no PGD is open.
- 0x04100010 answers the descriptor's data size as its result, or 0x80510206 while no PGD is open. Its seek refuses
  one before a PGD is open (0x80510206), and works in the data, stopping at its end (part 97).
- 0x04100002 keeps where the PGD starts (its sub_E3C): the same place again changes nothing; another closes any PGD
  open, until a key opens one there.
- PPSSPP's notes agree on the device (the key request is answered for any file), answer a PGD header that won't open
  0x80510204 ("likely a key mismatch"), and go on with 0 for a file without PGD's magic, read as it is.
- A game asks for the wrong key's refusal: Black Wolves Saga gives INSTALL2.DNS first the key it gave INSTALL.DNS
  (from the same 16 bytes), and on the refusal the 16 bytes after them, which open it (below). Master answered 0 to
  the first, `pgd.cpp` recovering the right key from the header's MAC.

**The change** (`io.cpp`, `pgd.cpp`, `pgd.hpp`, `kernel.hpp`).
- `ioctl()`: a memory stick file opened with 0x40000000 takes the PGD layer's three requests; one opened without it
  still takes none (0x8001b000), and a disc file takes them however it was opened, as before.
- The key (`pgdUnlock()`): the header read where the PGD starts, on either device (part 97's `pgdFileLength()` and
  `pgdFileRead()`), and checked at once, as the PGD layer checks it. Cut short or damaged (the DNAS MAC), or a
  descriptor putting the data past its file: 0x80510204. A key its 0x70 MAC refuses: 0x80510206, no key recovered.
  Refused, the file stays locked, reading as it is, and keeps where its PGD starts for another key; unlocked, it reads
  as its data from then on, as before. `pgd.cpp`'s two MAC checks are named for it (`Pgd::intact()`,
  `Pgd::keyMatches()`) and `Pgd::descriptor()` uses them; it still recovers the version key where no key was
  checked, which since the review's round is sceNpDrmEdataSetupKey's EDATA alone (its licensee key isn't the version
  key: part 97).
- 0x04100002 (the review's round), as the PGD layer keeps it (the decompilation's sub_E3C): given where the PGD
  starts already, nothing changes; given anywhere else, no PGD is open until a key opens one there. It used to mark the
  file as a PGD with no key, and the next read, seek, 0x04100010 or sceNpDrmEdataGetDataSize unlocked it with the key
  `pgd.cpp` recovered from its header (part 97's, on the stick's flagged files too in the first round). An unlocked
  file keeps where its data starts, not its PGD, so its own key tells whether the place given is its PGD's: the PGD
  that key opens there, its data where it was.
- The PGD layer's three requests on a descriptor open to write (the review's round): 0x80510201, as its open refuses
  one. Only a state saved before that refusal holds one (master's `openFile()` took 0x40000003).
- A file without PGD's magic given a key reads as it is, answered 0, on the stick as on the disc: master's choice for
  7th Dragon 2020's fan translations (part 51's fix 2: their INSDIR data is decrypted, and they take anything but
  success as the drive failing), whose GAME.DNS this library's 7th Dragon 2020 installs as it is ("CPK " at its start).
  The PGD layer answers 0x80510204 there.
- 0x04100010: the data's size, or 0x80510206 while no PGD is unlocked.
- `openFile()`: a file opened with 0x40000000 to write is refused (0x80510201) on either device, before it's made or
  emptied. So the PGD path never writes a player's files, and a PGD is still never a descriptor that emptied its file
  (part 97's rule, now over the stick's PGDs too).
- The disc's seek request (0x01010005) on an unlocked PGD works in its data, as sceIoLseek does: from its end, the
  data's; past the data's end refused (0x80010005), as past a plain file's end. On a PSP the PGD layer passes that
  request to the disc's driver, which works on the raw file and a position of its own; Phobos keeps one position, an
  unlocked PGD's in its data, as its reads and seeks have it. None of the games traced sends it on a PGD file
  (Gunhound EX, 7th Dragon 2020 and part 97's seven UMD PGD games; part 97's survey covered 41 of the library's 266).

**Tests** (tests/psp/disc.cpp, three new groups and three changed; the review's round two more, one in files.cpp,
and one grown).
- `memory stick PGD files through the PGD layer`: a PGD of 5000 bytes in 1 KiB blocks, MAC type 1 (as Gunhound EX's),
  at Gunhound EX's path, opened with 0x40000001. Locked: it reads as it is, ends where the file does, and 0x04100010
  refuses (0x80510206). Its key: 0. Its size from 0x04100010, sceNpDrmEdataGetDataSize and its end, the data's;
  sceIoGetstat, the file's. Read whole, and at 13 starts by 6 sizes across its 16-byte and 1 KiB blocks and its end;
  sought past the end (stopping there), back from where it is and from its end; a second key, a wrong one, leaves it
  unlocked; a state saved there loads and reads on; the key and a read made asynchronously (opened with 0x40004001, as
  7th Dragon 2020 opens its GAME.DNS); its host file unchanged.
- `memory stick PGD files refused`: a wrong key (0x80510206, the file then as it is until its own key unlocks it); a
  damaged header, one cut short and a descriptor past its file (0x80510204, each left as it is); a short key
  (0x8001b000, as on the disc); a CPK file and a 2-byte one given a key (0, read as they are, no data size); a file
  opened without 0x40000000 (the three requests 0x8001b000); four ways of opening with 0x40000000 to write (0x80510201,
  the file unchanged and none made); a PGD 0x800 bytes into its file by 0x04100002, a wrong key then its own; every
  file byte for byte as it was.
- `PGD files' disc seek requests stop at their data's end`: a UMD PGD with block MACs after its data. Locked, the
  file's end; unlocked, the data's (3000, not 3208); 100 back reads the last 100 bytes; the disc's read request
  (0x01030008) from 2500 reads 500; back to 0; to 3000 taken; to 3001, or past the end from it, refused.
- Changed: `disc PGD keys` (a "\0PGD" file without a PGD's MACs: 0x80510204, where it was 0; a disc file opened with
  0x40000000 to write: 0x80510201, where it was 0x8001b004); `disc PGD reads` (a wrong key: 0x80510206 and the file as
  it is, then its own key, where the recovered key gave 0 and the data; 0x04100010); and `download DRM on an EDATA
  beside files emptied as they're opened` (files.cpp: the EDATA is emptied through a plain write descriptor, 0x0602,
  as 0x40000602's is now refused, which is checked with the EDATA unchanged).
- Against master (`6ff82f9f1` with these tests and the three error names, unsanitized): the six fail, 152 checks (the
  stick's 108, the refusals' 28, the disc seek's 7, the disc reads' 5, the EDATA's 2, the disc keys' 2), and the
  other 552 pass. The branch: 558 groups, 0 failures.
- The review's round. `where a memory stick PGD starts, as the PGD layer keeps it (0x04100002)` (new): three PGDs in
  one file, the first under one key, the next two under another. Given alone, the first's start, then the second's:
  no data size (0x80510206), the file's end and bytes; the first's key refused there (0x80510206), the second's
  taking it. Unlocked: the second's start again keeps it, reading on where it was; the third's (which the same key
  opens) and then the first's (which it doesn't) leave none open, each opened then by its own key. `download DRM on
  an EDATA given the PGD layer's requests` (new, files.cpp): readied by sceNpDrmEdataSetupKey, its PGD's start (0x90)
  keeps it readied; readied on another descriptor and given a key that isn't its PGD's (the licensee key) before
  anything is read: 0x80510206, no data size, the file's size and bytes, until its PGD's key opens it. And `memory
  stick PGD files refused` gains the disc's own five requests on a flagged file (where it is, a seek, its first sector,
  its size, a read: 0x8001b000) and a descriptor open to write with the flag (put on it, as an older state holds one:
  the three requests 0x80510201).
- Each pinned against a mutation (one build with switches; the PGD, EDATA and state groups run): 0x04100002 as it was
  (the file marked, no key): 13 checks fail; the review's one-line fix alone (`open.pgd = open.pgd &&
  open.pgdReady`): 7 (an unlocked file moved to the third PGD's start kept open, one moved to the first's unlocked

  0 failures.

**Games** (`~/phobos-work/scratch/pgd-stick`: master's runner and the branch's, built from `bd4b4c058`'s code before two
comments changed; the runner's file I/O trace, the clock pinned, deep play's boot scripts; the sticks APFS

## Part 102: Vulkan at 5x on the RP6 — what grows with the resolution (the scene passes' hidden pixels, shaded because the shader writes the depth; Activision Hits' depth copies through the staging buffer), the depth-writing shader's depth declared never above the depth rasterized, another frame buffer's depth taken image to image

On branch `cursor/psp-hires-2b67` (draft PR #265), on master `a8d5640f5` (part 101, #263), master `7023fb080` (#264, no
part) merged in. The 5x collapse the nightly sweep found on the RP6, found out game by game on the M1 with a measurement
build and then on the RP6 itself (the coordinator's runs: no agent touches the RP6). Clean room: no PPSSPP for the GE or
GPU code, JPCSP not read; for what Turnip does, Mesa's documentation and Igalia's write-up of Adreno's low-resolution Z.
Save states: unchanged.

**The problem.** The sweep (nightly-215681, the owner's profile, Turnip v37, Vulkan fast) at 5x against 1x: Activision
Hits 57.6 → 2.9 fps, Chains of Olympus 59.6 → 9.8, Ghost of Sparta 36.8 → 10.8, Killzone 59.7 → 24.0, Super Monkey
Ball Adventure 35.6 → 26.3, Army of Two: The 40th Day 42.5 → 25.6, Colin McRae Rally 59.2 → 52.9; the HUD in the 5x
shots had the GPU 93-98% busy at 615-680 MHz and the CPU at 7-19%.

**What grows with the resolution** (the M1, MoltenVK, Vulkan fast, late frames as the app presents them, 120 frames;
a scratch build with a timestamp query before each pass of draws and each other command, `~/phobos-work/scratch/
psp-hires/patches/gputime-patch.py`):
- Nothing on the CPU: no finish or read back a frame, the CPU's conversions under 0.1 ms a frame, the emulation
  thread's instructions flat from 1x to 5x (Chains of Olympus 100 → 107 million); the CPU waits for the GPU.
- The GPU's milliseconds a frame, 1x → 5x, are the passes of draws: Chains of Olympus 18.5 → 138.6 (passes 10.0 →
  124.0: its scene, one pass of 37 draws, 36 meshes of 6,500 triangles, every one depth-tested, 2-4 ms at 1x and
  47-49 at 5x), Ghost of Sparta 19.0 → 148.0 (136.1), Army of Two 23.8 → 87.8 (75.3), Killzone 28.1 → 86.0 (76.1),
  Super Monkey Ball 13.6 → 71.0 (62.8), Activision Hits' copyright screen 10.4 → 86.1 (62.0, and its depth copies
  4.5 → 23.7).
- Those passes' fragments: every pipeline whose depth test or write depends on the depth takes `draw.frag`'s `DEPTHS`
  build (part 83), which writes the GE's whole number as `gl_FragDepth`; the GPU tests such a depth after the shader,
  so every hidden pixel is shaded, its texels filtered in the shader. Without that build (timing only: the pictures
  aren't exact) Chains of Olympus at 5x ran 7.3 → 13.4 fps on the M1 and 9.6 → 19.1 on the RP6. A Metal System
  Trace of it: 18.2 s of fragment work in a 21.9 s run.
- Chains of Olympus draws its scene two or three times a vblank (below). Activision Hits' copyright screen loops
  about ten times a vblank over three frame buffers that share a depth buffer: 28 whole-screen depth copies a frame
  (`Command::Depth`, 98.7 million pixels a frame at 5x, through the run's staging buffer) and 42 whole-target blended
  quads.

**The RP6** (the coordinator's runs of a measurement build, `rp6/hires-rp6.sh`: 150 frames, two rounds, the best of
them; Turnip StevenMXZ v26.3.0 loaded as the app loads its own, and Qualcomm's driver; fps, with the GPU's ms a frame):

| 5x, Turnip | master | the declaration | no DEPTHS (inexact) | render areas | depth image to image |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chains of Olympus (menu) | 9.6 / 103.2 | 9.8 / 100.5 | 19.1 / 51.2 | 9.8 / 100.4 | 10.1 / 97.9 |
| Ghost of Sparta (menu) | 8.9 / 111.8 | 8.9 / 111.8 | 10.6 / 92.9 | 8.9 / 111.7 | 9.2 / 107.6 |
| Super Monkey Ball (story) | 13.4 / 72.2 | 14.2 / 68.3 | 15.3 / 63.3 | 14.3 / 67.6 | 15.8 / 61.0 |
| Killzone (play) | 15.8 / 61.4 | 16.0 / 60.8 | 17.1 / 56.8 | 16.1 / 60.4 | 16.0 / 60.8 |
| Army of Two (play) | 14.9 / 65.4 | 14.9 / 65.4 | 18.8 / 51.6 | 15.0 / 65.1 | 15.8 / 61.4 |
| Activision Hits (copyright) | 2.7 / 373.7 | 2.7 / 373.7 | 3.1 / 324.4 | 2.7 / 374.0 | 19.3 / 50.9 |

(The declaration there is the measurement build's, both directions, below; "render areas" and "image to image" have
it too.) At 1x nothing changed (Chains of Olympus 127.7 / 128.3 fps). Qualcomm's driver: the declaration +1-2%, its
passes slower than Turnip's everywhere (Chains of Olympus 106 against 92 ms) but its staging copies of depth fast
(Activision Hits 12.9 fps at 5x, 28 ms of depth copies against Turnip's 331). Everything at 5x is the GPU's (Chains
of Olympus 17.5 ms of CPU a frame against 103 of GPU).

### The depth declared never above the depth rasterized

`draw.frag`'s `DEPTHS` build declares `layout(depth_less) out float gl_FragDepth`: the depth it writes, the GE's whole
number floor(z) / 65536, is never above the depth the GPU rasterizes. Rasterized as the GE's, z / 65535, it's above the
whole number by z / 65535 - floor(z) / 65536, nothing at 0 and k / 65536 of a step at whole number k; so the pipelines
that take the declared build rasterize it a step and a half above, (z + 1.5) / 65536.5 (`draw.vert`'s and
`transform.vert`'s specialization constant `ABOVE`, set by `pipelineFor()`): the whole number lies a step below it at
least wherever the GPU's depth and the depth interpolated beside it part by less than a step, and every corner's depth
rasterized lies within 0-1 (1.0 at 65535). That holds where the corners' depths are the GE's 0-65535 (a float's step at
65535 is 1/256 of one; every 3D corner's is held there). So the declared build is taken only there, and only where the
device clamps depth (`Backend::depthBuild()` says how each pipeline was made); a 2D PRIM with a corner's depth past
0-65535 (through mode's float positions, unheld: `Pipeline::outside`, which `emit()` decides for each primitive, every
corner weighing) and every pipeline of a device without depth clamping take the build undeclared, the depth rasterized
at the GE's, as before this part: its `DepthLess` execution mode taken out of the SPIR-V as the backend starts
(`GPU::undeclared()`), which leaves master's `DEPTHS` fragment SPIR-V word for word, and `ABOVE` off in the vertex
shaders, master's arithmetic (their SPIR-V carries the constant). Leaving out the devices without clamping is caution,
not need: the margin would fit there too (a declared corner's depth rasterized is at most (65535 + 1.5) / 65536.5, 1.0
exactly, inside the clip volume), but no such device has run these pipelines (MoltenVK, lavapipe, Turnip and Qualcomm's
driver all clamp). The review found the case: a 2D quad with corners at -9.9 million, 9.8 million, 5.3 million and -5.3
million (a float's step there is a whole one), drawn always and written, then again with "greater or equal", kept 1 of
384 pixels of the first drawing at 1x and 2 of 1,536 at 2x on MoltenVK, in both modes, and none with the declaration
taken out. A GPU that takes the declaration may reject, before the shader runs, a fragment a greater or greater-or-equal
test fails, as it would fail it after. Metal takes it, and Turnip in part: Super Monkey Ball's scene, tested greater or
equal, has its passes 63.2 → 59.3 ms a frame at 5x on the RP6 (53.9 with no depth written at all), the other scenes'
(less or less-or-equal) the same; Qualcomm's driver doesn't (its passes 70.6 ms either way). It costs nothing where it
isn't taken (the same pipelines, the same SPIR-V but for the declaration).

What `ABOVE` moves on MoltenVK: a 2D corner whose depth is rasterized outside 0-1 moves the depth Metal interpolates
beside it (`vertexDepth`), which the shader writes from, by where that corner is rasterized; with `ABOVE` such a quad
wrote other depths than master's (the review's quad with corners from -30000 to 65535, drawn and then redrawn "equal"
by a pipeline without `ABOVE`, differed at 247 of 384 pixels). Inside 0-65535 nothing moves (the review read back
every depth of four in-range 2D quads at 1x and 5x, with and without `ABOVE`: the same), nor in 3D. Those quads take
the undeclared pipelines now, rasterized at the GE's, so their depths are master's again. One corner the declaration
doesn't cover: `transform.vert`'s corner behind the camera (w ≤ 0), rasterized at the GE's without the margin, which
only the GPU's own rounding of a corner the GE found in front could make (`meshTriangles()` cuts every triangle with
one before the GPU sees it).

What was tried and left out: a "never below" build for less and less-or-equal tests, which Chains of Olympus, Ghost of
Sparta, Army of Two and Killzone draw their scenes with (Super Monkey Ball tests "greater or equal"), the one that gave
the M1 its gain (Chains of Olympus at 5x 7.2 → 12.3 fps, its scene pass 47 → 18-19 ms). Its depth rasterized must lie
below the whole number, which is 0 for any depth below 1: a corner's depth rasterized below 0 (clamped per pixel), or
the declaration untrue. The test below found both wrong on the M1: a 2D depth past 65535 clamped to 1.0, above the
65535 written (fixed by holding it first); and a 3D floor with the depth range turned around, its far corners' depth
0.73, whose less-or-equal strip lost whole rows to the first drawing, at 1x and 2x, in both modes — with no
declaration at all too: MoltenVK moves the depth interpolated beside a corner rasterized below 0 (depthClampEnable
or not; nothing's clipped, every pixel is drawn), and whole numbers flip where the depth is steep. Held at 0, the
corner's depth makes the declaration untrue wherever the held corner weighs in (a coplanar less-or-equal redraw then
loses pixels). Exact on any GPU, it would need a depth encoding with room below 0 (below, Left).

**The tests** (`tests/psp/gpu.cpp`). "gpu depth a GPU may test before the shader runs": the builds' SPIR-V execution
modes (DEPTHS and SINGLE DEPTHS DepthReplacing and DepthLess, the others none, the DEPTHS builds undeclared
DepthReplacing alone); then the same triangles drawn twice, the first time written with "always", the second tested
with each comparison, every comparison over a strip of its own, their depths across all of 0-65535: always, equal, at
most and at least draw over every pixel the first drew, the others over none. In both modes, at 1x and 2x: 2D strips
against the software renderer, 2D depths past 65535 (at most, equal and at least over 65535, where the GPU clamps
depth: the capability `vulkan-depth-clamp`, which CI's lavapipe lanes require), and a 3D floor from the near plane to
the far one, its depth 36-65534 along it, the depth range either way. It fails on the measurement build's both-ways
placement (the two cases above). "gpu depth past 0-65535 in 2D": the review's quad through a pretend backend (its
draw's key `outside`; one in range not; a quad below 0 alone, and a triangle whose first corner is in range and another
past 65535, `outside` too, so every corner weighs on either side of the range, which the second round asked for, as
Metal shows no picture of those two; nor one whose depth decides nothing, nor fast mode's mesh), then drawn twice as
above, every comparison over a strip of its own (the greater-or-equal strip the corners above), at 1x-5x in both
modes: it fails on MoltenVK without `outside`. "gpu depth's pipelines": `depthBuild()` for every comparison, written or
not, in 2D and fast mode's 3D, in range and past it: declared and raised together exactly where the device clamps and
the corners are in range, so a pipeline with the declaration but not the margin fails it (the margin taken away, or
only for greater or equal: the review's two mutations, which no picture on the M1 shows, its two interpolations being
that close in range); and two renderers with depth clamping turned off before they make a pipeline (as a device without
it makes them), whose pipelines are all undeclared and which draw the first test's 2D strips and 3D floor as the GE
does. The margin's size isn't pinned, and the M1 can't pin it: with a scratch constant for it, a margin of nothing or
of half a step passes every test there and all of the review's 21 sets of strips (only a negative one fails, in
gpuDepthEarly); the M1 shows whether the margin is applied, not that a step and a half is enough.

### Another frame buffer's depth taken image to image

`takeDepth()`'s `Command::Depth` (part 90) copied the other target's depth into the buffer and out into this one's, as
MoltenVK's copy between images of their depth aspect alone takes the stencil too, where the stencil is each frame
buffer's own. Now it's copied from image to image (`vkCmdCopyImage`, the depth aspect alone, the same regions and runs)
where the device's such copy is found to leave the stencil (`Backend::depthAlone`); elsewhere the staging buffer as
before, no room reserved in it where it isn't used. `depthAloneProbe()`, as the backend starts, writes three 128x64
pictures of the depth format from a buffer (none a cleared picture, which a driver may copy another way), each depth and
stencil a pattern of its own, the depths no whole steps of either format (a copy must keep them bit for bit), then
copies the first's depth into the second whole and into the third as a part, 45x27 from (5, 3) to (37, 9), placed and
sized as no tile or block is, as a run's copy is partial and offset; it reads both back and wants the depth taken inside
the part and every other depth and every stencil as they were. A probe the GPU doesn't finish loses the device as
`wait()` does (the fence, the command buffer and the pictures it may still use left as they are); a device lost
otherwise lets its pictures and buffers go. The same depths either way (a copy of the same format's depth values); the
stencil left as far as the probe sees, a whole copy and a partial one of pictures written by uploads, not drawn (the
RP6's saved states, below, check the copies games make). Not on the M1: MoltenVK's copy takes the stencil (Metal copies
a depth and stencil picture whole), and so does lavapipe's (the first push of this work had the copy on every device but
a portability implementation, and CI's lavapipe lanes failed gpuSharedDepth's stencil bytes, 0x5a expected, the other
frame buffer's 0xa5, every depth right). On the RP6 both probes find the copy leaves the stencil, with Turnip and with
Qualcomm's driver alike: the first (the whole copy alone) and the new one, with the part (the fix round's build: "image
copy 1" in every run, at 1x and 5x on Turnip and at 5x on Qualcomm's driver, the depth format D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT on
both), so both copy image to image. The tests that take depth between frame buffers (gpuSharedDepth: each its own
stencil; gpuDepthOrders: the runs between an 8888 frame buffer and a 16-bit one, at 1x and 2x) pass either way. Where
the probe says no (the M1, CI's lavapipe), both force the copy as well: gpuSharedDepth once, finding the stencil taken
as the probe said, and gpuDepthOrders every way it's run, every byte of the screens the software renderer's, so the
copy's regions and runs are tested where the probe declines it (each run's offsets swapped fail it); and every image
copy's aspects are counted (`Backend::depthCopyAspects`), the depth's alone wanted, as a copy naming the stencil too
looks the same on a device that takes the stencil anyway. Activision Hits' copyright screen on the RP6 (the fix round's
build, below): at 5x 2.7 → 19.4 fps on Turnip, its depth copies 331.6 → 8.3 ms of GPU time a frame, and 12.9 → 16.7 fps
on Qualcomm's driver (28.5 → 11.1 ms); at 1x 15.4 → 247.0 fps on Turnip.

### Exactness

The 21 kit scenes and five more (Hot Wheels' race, Killzone's play and menu, MX vs. ATV's ride, Chains of Olympus'
menu), 100 frames each, every frame's picture and VRAM once its drawing settled, then RAM and the machine's state: the
same as master's at 1x in all three renderers, and at 5x, with Activision Hits' copyright screen, in both Vulkan modes:
every hash the same (26 scenes x 3 renderers, 27 x 2), on 3c20bdbf5 and again on the fix round's code (77143a9ff). None
of those scenes draws a 2D PRIM past 0-65535 whose depth decides (master and the fix make the same draws, primitives and
pipelines in all 106 Vulkan runs, the second review found), so the hashes don't reach those pipelines; the coordinator's
Vulkan library check of the games on ad226f623 does. On the M1 the depth goes through the staging buffer (the probe's
no), so the image copy was checked on the RP6: the states saved at frame 120 at 5x on Turnip by master's build and
3c20bdbf5's (RAM, VRAM and the machine, as the GPU leaves them; on the M1 the same file run to run) are the same file
for Activision Hits' copyright screen, Chains of Olympus' menu and Super Monkey Ball's story. The coordinator's targeted
check of 3c20bdbf5's image copy over the library (the six scenes from their states at 5x and 2x, the 8 games that take
another frame buffer's depth most from boot at 5x, and the 217 that take it more than 30 times in their first 900 frames
at 2x, each saved after its takes, on Turnip; the copy's code is the same in the fix round) found every pair the same
file: 237 of 237, none different, none missing (18:50-20:28, `rp6/hires-takes-rp6-summary.txt`, every run of this
branch's build saying "image copy 1"). The fix round's build (77143a9ff) against master's again
(`rp6b/hires-fix-rp6-states.txt`, `rp6b/hires-takes-fix-rp6.log`): the states at frame 150 at 5x of all six scenes of
the speed runs below are the same file on Turnip and on Qualcomm's driver, the image copy taken in every run of the fix
on both; and the targeted check's first 20 pairs (the six scenes from their states at 5x and 2x, the 8 heaviest games
from boot at 5x) are 20 the same, none different, none missing. tests/psp: 576 groups, 0 failures (sanitized).

### The review's round

An independent review asked for changes, and the fix round (77143a9ff, 47e0c5d74) made them: the declaration only where
its proof holds (above: B1, the 2D quad near ten million; B2, devices without depth clamping); the image copy's regions
and aspect pinned where the probe declines it (gpuDepthOrders forced, `Backend::depthCopyAspects`); the margin pinned
(`Backend::depthBuild()`); the probe's timeout handled as `wait()`'s and its copy made partial and unaligned too
(above); and these sections corrected where they said more than was so. Each of the review's mutations and the round's
own now fails a committed test on the M1: the margin removed, or removed for greater or equal, or the declaration kept
without clamping (gpuDepthBuilds); the declaration kept past 0-65535 (gpuDepthBuilds, and gpuDepthOutside loses the
review's very pixels, 1 of 384 at 1x and 2 of 1,536 at 2x); `emit()` not marking those PRIMs (gpuDepthOutside); the copy
naming both aspects (gpuSharedDepth, gpuDepthOrders); its offsets swapped (gpuDepthOrders, 2,048 and 9,080 bytes apart).
The second round approved, with two should-fixes: the new probe on the RP6 (met: the fix round's build took the image
copy on both drivers, its states master's; below), and `emit()`'s test of every corner, on either side of the range:
corners below 0 unseen, or only the first corner looked at, passed every test, Metal showing no picture of either; the

### Chains of Olympus' scenes a vblank: ours

Its menu draws its scene two or three times a vblank (the same 37 draws each time, in fast and accurate mode alike), and
each costs the host its drawing at 5x. That's the GE's time (part 62's): Chains of Olympus' loop never waits for the
vertical blank (sceGeListSync of the last frame's list, the frame shown at once, the next queued), so it draws as often
as the GE finishes, and geTime() charges a list Sony's peak figures, a lower bound: about 4.2 million pixels a scene
at four a clock, 6.3 ms at 166 MHz, 2.6 scenes a vblank. A PSP's GE is slower and draws fewer (part 62's "Left"): the
owner's PSP-1000 (6.61, ARK) drew 357 lists, 357 syncs and 357 flips in each of two 10-second windows on Chains of
Olympus' menus (UCAS40198, no vblank waits), about 36 a second or 0.6 a vblank, where Phobos draws this menu's scene
2.6 times a vblank (about 156 a second); his captures of this scene itself are to come (the profiler's second phase
compares them). At one pixel a clock it would be 0.65 a vblank, a quarter of the host's work now. The way there is a
round of measurements on the owner's PSP (fills textured and not, 16- and 32-bit, triangles of a few sizes, transfers,
timed around sceGeDrawSync) and geTime() from them: GE timing, not the renderer's.

### Left

- **The shader's depth write on Adreno**, the RP6's biggest cost (without it, timing only, Chains of Olympus +100%,
  Army of Two +26%, Ghost of Sparta +20%, Activision Hits +15%, Super Monkey Ball +14%, Killzone +8%). Taking the depth
  from the GPU's fixed function (that build left out, D16 rounding, a shifted depth with a shifted comparison,
  gl_FragCoord.z) decides whole numbers by another interpolator than the shader's, and where the two straddle one the
  pixel differs. Exact ways, designed, none made: flat draws (every corner one depth) without the write, their depth
  rasterized as the whole number written (a constant interpolates exactly, as master's shader already assumes); the
  shader reading the depth as it is (rasterization order) and discarding before its texels where the GE's comparison
  fails, a failure that changes nothing else (stencil); Turnip doing more with the declaration than it does now
  (Super Monkey Ball's greater-or-equal scene gets 3.9 of the 9.3 ms not writing the depth saves; the measurement
  build's never-below half gave Chains of Olympus' less-or-equal scene 2.7 of 52), in the app's own Turnip; and the
  "never below" build exact on any GPU with an encoding with room below 0 and above 65535 (floor(z) + K over 2^17,
  every corner's depth within 0-1), which changes the depth's conversions (`GPU::depthToFloat()` and the rest,
  `copy.frag`, `move.frag`).
- Render areas over what a pass's draws reach: the RP6 +0-1% (Chains of Olympus' passes 388 → 119 a frame, its GPU
  time the same), so not made.
- A 2D corner's depth past 0-65535 is clamped per pixel on the GPU (the software renderer holds each corner's), as
  before.
